name: painted_steel
summary: MU's metal as MU drew it: a bright highlight painted down the middle of a dark blade, and no reflectance to speak of.
why: Metallic 0.0 on something that is obviously metal, which needs the argument.
A metal has no diffuse at all - what you see is its reflectance tinting whatever it
reflects - so a metallic material's base colour is its F0, and iron's is 0.56 in linear.
MU's metal sheets are nowhere near that. steel.jpg averages 0.083, steel_barred_a 0.066,
steel_barred_b 0.015. They are not measurements of reflectance; they are paintings, with
the highlight drawn in and everything around it left dark.
Handed to a renderer as metal, that produces a metal darker than any that exists, and what
comes back is black chrome reflecting a sky. It gets away with it on a thin bar seen against
bright ground, where the eye reads a silhouette - which is why Lorencia's railings looked
right - and it does not on a broad flat surface, which is where it was caught: House02 is a
crate of tools and its blades came back black.
So metallic 0 and roughness 0.28. The painted highlight survives as albedo, the renderer
adds a real one on top of it, and the thing reads as polished steel because that is what
the artist drew. It is the same call lamplight and foliage needed and for the same reason:
MU's art has its lighting in it, and a material that ignores that is fighting the picture.
Depth 0.08 and range 0.05, both small. A blade is smooth and what varies across it is the
highlight, which is already in the colour.
wrought_iron keeps metallic 1.0 and does not move to this, which is not an inconsistency
left lying about. Its sheet is 0.066 - lower than this one - and rendered both ways the
railing is black iron at metallic 1 and pale brass rod at metallic 0. The line between the
two materials is whether the dark in the sheet is the subject or the background: bars painted
black are the subject, and the ground around a painted highlight is not.
A warning about where this does not belong, because the argument above reads as though it
belongs anywhere MU painted a metal. Metallic 0.0 with a dark sheet means there is almost
nothing for a light to do: the lit render comes out equal to the unshaded one and the item
reads as matte black plastic. That is fine on a thin bar seen against bright ground, which
is what this was written for and what its remaining wearer is. On a broad dark surface -
a shield's face, a cuirass - it removes the lighting rather than fixing the colour, and
plate_steel is the answer. Four pieces in one batch were assigned here on the strength of
this file and all four wanted plate_steel.
The grain is the other half of the trap: brushed along v, which stripes any face wider than
a bar. The Kite Shield hit that before it hit the darkness. See Shield03's material_note,
which records all four attempts.
